title: Distinct silhouettes per ore tier: swords, pickaxes, axes, hammers, bows
player_outcome: Copper, iron, gold, demonite, hellstone and the hardmode tiers each have their own recognisable shapes: stubby copper picks, ornate gold guards, spiky evil blades, a flaming molten pick. They are no longer the same mesh in a new colour.
design: Verified: all 42 swords are one 88-tri 5-vertex blade (items.py:22-25); picks, axes and hammers take only a tint; all 17 {metal}_bow share limbLayer iron.

New bgen/blade_profiles.py: named 2D blade profiles (straight, leaf, broad, katana, curved, serrated, hooked, jagged, cleaver, rapier), guards (bar, crescent, winged, disc, none) and pommels (ball, gem, ring).
items.sword becomes profile-driven: params profile, guard, pommel, fuller (bool), edge (hex), gem, curve (bend via bmesh). shortsword uses rapier/leaf.
Pick, axe and hammer heads get style variants: stubby, straight, ornate, spiky, flame. Picks are an extruded curved polygon with a bevel (not a 6-segment tube); hammers a bevelled lathe head.
Bows get limb curvature, tip ornaments and a grip wrap colour per style.

assets.json 'metalStyles' {metal: {sword, guard, pick, axe, hammer, bow}}: copper/tin simple, iron/lead straight, silver/tungsten fuller, gold/platinum ornate, demonite/crimtane spiky, hellstone flame, cobalt/palladium, mythril/orichalcum, adamantite/titanium distinct hardmode shapes. build_all.plan merges a metal's style into the pattern params.
Keep items.py under 400 lines: move tool heads into a new bgen/tools_heads.py if needed. Budget 200–800 tris.
